writer_cursor_base_capture.scope: Base and overlay are warmed; first overlay promotion remains O(N log N), ordinary point-only writers retain the flat hash path.

run_handle_index_lookup.scope: Two Debug timing samples for isolated handle lookup, not query throughput. Both paths use a real cached table index.

async_candidate_planning.scope: Candidate state only; fixed in-flight slots replace per-key state, resolution flags, and materialized key/run pairs. Payload IO and cache handles retain their existing costs.

directory_all_mutable_overlapping_runs.measurement: Before: isolated review fixture. After: once-per-key classification; run traversal excludes resolved keys.

shared_decode_optional_oom_fallback.before: point fails OutOfMemory despite successful direct lookup
shared_decode_optional_oom_fallback.after: direct lookup succeeds; optional decode retry disabled; checksum failures preserved

shared_sparse_prefix_decode.prefix_snappy_strategy_after: decode prefix records once, reuse restart lookup; no full raw-row expansion
shared_sparse_prefix_decode.scope: two distant points; optional cache bounded to 64 KiB per block and 256 KiB per batch

single_user_snappy_result_retention.scope: Owned result payload only: 64 one-byte values; batch cache and descriptor arrays are separate. Single-point callers that retain key hints still own rows; async batches do not retain keys or namespaces.

mandatory_async_decode_budget.before: lookup succeeds through an uncharged C allocation
mandatory_async_decode_budget.after_resource_denial: ResourceBudgetExceeded; read-working-set usage returns to zero
checks: admitted fallback succeeds and releases scratch
actual shared-prefix batch rejects required key scratch when read budget is exhausted
optional decode-cache denial still permits an admitted direct reader

prefix_reader_reuse.comparison: independent prefix point lookups owning encoded rows versus production PrefixPointReader reuse with value-only results
prefix_reader_reuse.backing: native C allocator with allocation counters
prefix_reader_reuse.scope: Decoder and result-ownership microbenchmark. Times are Debug samples, not end-to-end throughput. Sparse requests use restart jumps; dense requests advance through their interval.

prefix_key_scratch_retention.exceptional_keys: temporary admitted key allocation; reader is discarded before reuse
prefix_key_scratch_retention.allocation_failure_retry: restart from the index; preserve bounded capacity

shared_sync_hot_prefix_promotion.scope: Native Debug helper fixture, MemoryStorage, C result allocator; before uses repeated physical-cache reads on the comparison head, after enables automatic promotion and attaches a resource manager. Timing samples are indicative, not end-to-end throughput or a controlled production benchmark. Targeted cases cover construction/retention denial, optional cache allocation failure, small-cache and transient bypass, invalidation with pinned values, concurrent promoter election and retry cooldown.

scope: Deterministic allocation, directory traversal, admission, and isolated Debug timing fixtures, not query throughput or a 2 GiB soak. Caller-owned mutable values, captured read-layout pointer arrays, payload IO/cache ownership, and first-use overlay promotion still have costs. Directory planning and index metadata reuse bounded resource-charged arenas; async candidate metadata has fixed stack storage.

arena_results.change: mandatory decode/key scratch uses a reclaimable runtime allocator independently of the result allocator; resource admission remains in lsm_read_working_set

large_singleton_snappy.eligibility: raw Snappy singleton above 64 KiB, value at least half the logical block, namespace and key fit a 4 KiB admission prefix
large_singleton_snappy.ownership: decode directly into final caller storage; retain the full singleton row including its small header and key; complete stream validation before publication
large_singleton_snappy.fallback: other shapes use reclaimable admitted scratch and selected-result copying

immutable_preclassification.covers: immutable values and tombstones, namespace separation; snapshot memtable precedence remains in the existing read path

scratch_lifetime_followup.validation_scope: native fixtures; directory selection counts are not an end-to-end throughput benchmark; no new 2 GiB soak

warm_decoded_prefix.returned_values: borrowed from retained decoded handles; callers preserve normal pin/value ownership

normal_miss.cold_prefix_miss: one physical load; no second full-block decode

sync_cache_followup.implementation: shared PointReadScratch admission and error translation; PrefixPointReader bounds and count validation; warm decoded-block lookup first; explicit handle ownership transfer; physical IO buffer released on checksum failure
sync_cache_followup.coverage: denied and admitted scratch, caller arena storage, warm reads under a denied scratch budget, namespace-preserving point semantics, invalid entry counts, corruption, result allocation failures, cache invalidation and returned-row lifetime
sync_cache_followup.scope: isolated native cache fixtures; not an end-to-end throughput or 2 GiB soak
